cycle.name: New 6-week cycle
focus: Cluster back squats (intra-set rest to preserve bar speed)
cycle.full_text:
NEW CYCLE, NEW 6 WEEK EXPERIMENT IN BECOMING HARDER TO KILL

This one has a few distinct focuses, and if you're someone who likes knowing why we keep making you do the same thing every week with tiny changes, welcome. This section is for you.

The big strength focus: back squats, but make them clusters. Rather than grinding through every rep continuously, we'll use short bouts of rest inside the set. Those little breaks aren't us being nice. Cluster sets can help preserve bar speed and power as fatigue accumulates, meaning more of your reps actually look like the strong, intentional reps we're trying to train—not the final squat where your soul briefly leaves your body. Research generally finds that cluster-style sets reduce velocity and power loss compared with traditional continuous sets.

Over six weeks, the goal is to accumulate high-quality strength work while progressively giving your body more to adapt to. And fun nerd fact: a 2026 study comparing six weeks of cluster and traditional back-squat training found similar improvements in strength and endurance, while the cluster group maintained better bar velocity and experienced less acute fatigue during training. Tiny rests. Legitimate science. We love to see it.

We're also spending time with the power snatch. The clue is very much in the name here: power. Olympic lifting asks you to produce force quickly, then coordinate a whole bunch of moving pieces before gravity notices what you're doing. Repeated exposure gives you time to refine those positions and timing instead of relearning the movement every few months. The goal isn't just eventually putting more weight overhead—it's making the whole thing feel more automatic along the way.

There's also a bigger emphasis on pulling and muscle-up skill work. And before anyone who doesn't have a muscle-up skips this paragraph: especially you. Skills like muscle-ups aren't magically unlocked the day you become "strong enough." They're a combination of pulling strength, body control, timing, coordination and lots of appropriately scaled practice. Wherever you're starting—ring rows, pull-ups, chest-to-bar, transitions, or full muscle-ups—there's something to build.

And finally, Tuesdays are getting a little makeover. You asked for more strength, we listened. Tuesdays will now give us more room to work on strength before moving into shorter, punchier conditioning instead of always asking you to settle in for the long haul.

That matters too. Fitness isn't just one energy system. Sometimes we want you learning to sustain work for 20 minutes. Sometimes we want you producing a lot of power for considerably less time and discovering that seven minutes can, in fact, feel longer than 20.

Different stimulus. Different adaptation. Same suspicious amount of sweating.

So that's our next six weeks: squat stronger, move the bar faster, build your pulling skills, and get comfortable working at a few different speeds.

Pick something you want to improve and pay attention to it now. We'll check back in six weeks.

Same humans. Slightly upgraded operating systems.

crossfit.name: CrossFit
crossfit.note: Week 1 of 6. Squat stronger, move the bar faster, build pulling skills, work at a few different speeds.

mon.title: Power snatch + 4 × 2:30 AMRAP

sections.label: Strength
lines: A1. Power Snatch — 4 sets of 2, building
A2. Feet-Elevated Parallette Push Up — 4 sets of 8–12

sections.label: Conditioning
lines: Handstand Push Ups with remaining time

mon.coach_notes:
We're kicking off the new cycle with power snatches + feet-elevated push-ups. For the snatches, think fast, not just heavy. Power is force produced quickly, so the goal is crisp extension, a decisive pull under the bar, and catching it high—not turning every rep into an accidental squat snatch because ambition got involved.

Then: four 2:30 intervals of DB snatches, double unders, and whatever time remains for handstand push-ups.

The trick? The HSPU are the score, but getting there recklessly is not the strategy. Keep the double unders around 30 seconds, keep the DB snatches moving, and arrive at the wall with enough shoulders left to actually do something useful.

You get a full minute between rounds, so aim for repeatable output—not one heroic opening round followed by three formal apologies.

tue.title: Cluster back squat + 8-min AMRAP

sections.label: Strength
lines: A. Cluster Back Squat — 5 sets of 2-2-1, building
B. Pendlay Row — 4 sets of 6–8, building

tue.coach_notes:
Cluster squats have arrived. Today's 2-2-1 means you'll complete five total reps per set, but with little intra-set breaks that let you reset, brace, and attack the next mini-set with more quality than you might have grinding through five straight.

Then we balance all that squatting with Pendlay rows before moving into our new Tuesday specialty: short and spicy.

Eight minutes.

Eight minutes is an interesting little purgatory: too long to truly sprint, short enough that you absolutely cannot get comfortable. The goal is a pace that feels slightly unreasonable but somehow sustainable from the beginning.

Our fittest athletes can chase 10 rounds. Everyone else: choose variations that let you keep moving and see how much work you can fit into eight very long minutes.

The workout is short. Your feelings about it may last longer.

wed.title: 4 × 10:00 HYROX-style pieces
wed.coach_notes:
Four 10-minute pieces today, and each follows the same sneaky little formula: do some work, do more work, then use whatever time remains to accumulate distance or calories.

The interesting part is deciding how much you're willing to spend to earn more time at the end. Move too casually through the buy-in and there's very little max-effort window left. Attack it like the building is on fire and you may arrive there with absolutely nothing to give.

That balance is useful HYROX practice. Racing isn't about being maximal everywhere; it's about knowing where you can push without borrowing too heavily from Future You.

You get two minutes between parts. Recover aggressively, then do it again.

Four opportunities to make excellent decisions while increasingly tired.

thu.title: RDL + pull skill, then row + 100 RKBS

sections.label: Strength
lines: A1. Romanian Deadlift — 4 sets of 6–8, building
A2. Pull-up / C2B / Bar Muscle-Up Practice — 4 sets

thu.coach_notes:
We're hinging with Romanian deadlifts today, then spending four sets working wherever you currently live on the pull-up → chest-to-bar → bar muscle-up spectrum.

And we really mean wherever you currently live. Skill practice works because of quality repetition. Your nervous system is learning timing and coordination every time you practice, whether today's rep is a kip swing, a strong pull-up, a transition drill, or a full muscle-up.

Then we remove basically all the fancy stuff:

2,000/1,600m row + 100 Russian kettlebell swings.

That's it. Suspiciously simple.

And simple conditioning has a beautiful way of revealing your actual fitness because there isn't much skill complexity to hide behind. Settle into a strong row, relax your grip, and have a plan for those swings before your forearms begin making decisions on your behalf.

Not glamorous. Extremely effective.

fri.title: Tempo cyclist squat + strict press, E2M × 9

sections.label: Strength
lines: A1. Goblet Cyclist Squat — 3 sets of 10–12 @ 31X1 tempo
A2. Strict Press — 3 sets of 8–10, building

fri.coach_notes:
First, tempo cyclist squats + strict press. The 31X1 tempo means three seconds down, one second at the bottom, stand with intent, reset at the top. Slowing the eccentric gives you more time under tension and, perhaps more importantly, nowhere to hide from your positions.

Then every two minutes for nine rounds:

5 hang power cleans
5 shoulder-to-overhead
5 push-ups / ring dips
15 air squats

…and the barbell gets heavier every three rounds.

The beautiful part is that your rest is whatever you earn. Move efficiently and you'll have close to a 1:1 work-to-rest ratio. Take unnecessary breaks and suddenly two minutes becomes an alarmingly short period of time.

The first three rounds should be unbroken and controlled. As the bar gets heavier, stay tidy rather than turning every clean into a small personal crisis.

Work. Rest. Add weight. Repeat.

sat.title: Run → work → run → work → run (hybrid, for time)

sections.label: Conditioning
lines: then 2 rounds: 25m Sled Push (5/3, 7/5 plates) · 25 Burpees · 25 Tuck Ups · 250m Ski
then 2 rounds: 25 KB Deadlifts (2×24/16 kg, 2×32/24 kg) · 25 Sandbag Reverse Lunges (20/10, 30/20 kg) · 25 AbMat Sit-ups · 250m Row

sat.coach_notes:
Saturday is giving us run → work → run → work → run, which is perhaps the purest expression of hybrid training imaginable.

You'll open with a 1.5-mile run, hit two rounds of sled pushes, burpees, tuck-ups and SkiErg, run another mile, then tackle KB deadlifts, sandbag lunges, sit-ups and rowing before finishing with another 1.5 miles.

So yes: today is about fitness. But it's also about gear shifting.

One of the most useful HYROX skills is learning to leave a station and run well before you feel fully recovered. Instead of standing around waiting for your heart rate to receive the memo, start running at a controlled pace and let the first few minutes become part of your recovery.

And please respect that opening run. There are approximately seventeen opportunities afterward to regret getting excited.

Start boring. Stay consistent. Get dangerous later.

Technically four miles of prescribed running, but emotionally? At least five.

athx.name: ATHX
athx.note: Test week — race-prep programming begins. Workouts mimic competition movements scaled to the 75-min (Tue) and 90-min (Sat) windows. ATHX Miami 10/10/26, Houston 10/17/26.

tue.title: ATHX 75 — test week

sections.label: ATHX MetCon / Endurance
lines: Station 5: 16 Plate-Elevated Dual DB Reverse Lunges (35/20) [Pro 50/25]

tue.coach_notes:
OKAY, ATHX CREW: WE'RE GETTING SPECIFIC.

With fall races getting closer, we're officially moving into race-prep programming. Up until now, we've been building the pieces: strength, endurance, power, work capacity, and the deeply important skill of continuing to make reasonable decisions while tired.

Now we start putting those pieces together in ways that look and feel a little more like race day.

That means you'll see more work around race-specific movements, transitions, pacing, compromised running/endurance, and maintaining output after fatigue has already entered the chat. Because being strong is useful. Having an engine is useful. The actual ATHX challenge is being able to access both when your legs have recently filed a complaint.

There's a fun training principle here called specificity: as competition gets closer, training should increasingly resemble the demands you're preparing for. We still want to build fitness, but now we're also practicing how to use that fitness—when to push, when to settle, how quickly to transition, and what pace you can actually repeat rather than the pace your ego suggested in minute two.

And if you're not racing? This is still an excellent block of hybrid training. Race prep doesn't mean you need a bib number to benefit from it. You're getting strong, powerful, aerobically fitter, and better at moving between very different demands without completely falling apart.

The fitness is built. Now we practice deploying it. Race season loading.

ATHX PROGRAMMING:

It's test week! Just over one month to go before the ATHX Competitions in Miami (10/10/26) and Houston (10/17/26)! Therefore, this week will feature workouts designed to closely mimic the competition movements scaled down to fit the 75-minute and 90-minute windows of our Tuesday and Saturday classes, respectively. Special shout out to those already signed up—and if you haven't and are interested in doing so, please check out the link in the newsletter to get involved in the US-based events and rep CrossFit NYC!

announcements.title: HYROX Simulation — Sat Sep 12
announcements.detail: CFNYC Upper West Side. $20 for members (+1 class credit for pack members). Email the Front Desk to register. Open to everyone.
announcements.full_text:
🚨 THIS SATURDAY: HYROX SIMULATION

Okay, people. This is it. FINAL CALL.

Our next CFNYC HYROX Simulation is happening THIS SATURDAY, September 12 at the Upper West Side, and this is your last newsletter reminder to stop thinking "I should probably sign up for that" and actually do it.

Whether you have a fall HYROX on the calendar, want to test the fitness you've been quietly building all summer, or are simply HYROX-curious and would like to find out what all the sled-related commotion is about—come play.

A simulation is one of the best opportunities to practice the stuff that's hard to recreate in a regular class: pacing, transitions, fueling, running on tired legs, and figuring out exactly how much enthusiasm is appropriate in the first 20 minutes. (Usually less than you think.)

📅 Saturday, September 12
📍 CFNYC Upper West Side
💰 $20 for members (plus one class credit for pack members)
📧 Email the Front Desk to register
🔥 Open to everyone

You do not need to be racing soon. You do not need to feel "ready." That is sort of the point.

Come test yourself. Come cheer ridiculously loudly for your friends. Come make some questionable sled decisions.

LAST CHANCE. Grab your spot. We'll see you Saturday. LFG.

announcements.title: 2027 CrossFit Open dates
announcements.full_text:
👀 THE OPEN IS COMING. LET'S BUILD SOMETHING.

We know February feels approximately 400 years away. It is not.

The 2027 CrossFit Open dates are officially on the calendar:

27.1 — February 18
27.2 — February 25
27.3 — March 4

And this year, we want CFNYC IN.

Not because we expect everyone to suddenly become a competitive CrossFit athlete. The Open is three weeks where the thing we do together all year gets a start line, a scorecard, and a whole lot more cheering.

It's also one of the best fitness check-ins we get. Do it year after year and suddenly you have actual data: Am I stronger? Is my engine better? Did the movement that stopped me last year become something I can do now? CrossFit specifically uses the Open as an annual benchmark for exactly that kind of progress.

So between now and February, pick a thing.

Maybe it's your first pull-up. Double unders. Toes-to-bar. Getting stronger with a barbell. Learning to pace instead of seeing God four minutes into an AMRAP.

Tell your coaches. Let us help you work on it.

Then, come February, we get to put all that training to use together.

Three workouts. Three weeks. One very loud CFNYC.

More Open hype incoming. Consider yourselves warned.

announcements.detail: Teams of two, end of October. Full details in next week's newsletter.
announcements.full_text:
SAVE THE DATE(ISH): CFNYC HALLOWEEN THROWDOWN 🎃

We have an idea. And because putting things in the newsletter makes them legally binding, we're doing it.

This October: The CFNYC Halloween In-House Competition. 👻🏋️

Think teams of two, CrossFit, costumes, questionable levels of competitiveness, and one very fun day with your CFNYC people.

Costumes are highly encouraged. And yes, we will be judging. Your fitness? Judged. Your teamwork? Judged. Your commitment to the bit? Absolutely judged.

There will be prizes. There will be bragging rights. There will be a Best Costume, because if you can figure out how to snatch dressed as Shrek, that deserves recognition.

For now, consider this your official heads-up: we're aiming for the end of October, with the exact date and full competition details coming in next week's newsletter.

So start finding your partner. Start plotting your costumes. Start casually asking your coach which friend complements your particular brand of fitness.

More details next week. For now: save the end of October and begin scheming.

announcements.title: Fall race season roll call
announcements.detail: Racing this fall (marathon, half, HYROX, ATHX, trail)? Tell your coaches or the Front Desk so the gym can show up and cheer.
announcements.full_text:
FALL RACE SEASON IS ON 🏁

The weather is about to get cooler, the training is getting suspiciously specific, and fall race season is officially upon us.

Marathons. Half marathons. HYROX. ATHX. Trail races. That slightly unhinged event your friend convinced you to sign up for six months ago and you are now realizing is, in fact, happening.

We want to know what you're doing.

One of our favorite things about CFNYC is that the fitness you build here goes out into the world with you—and we want to celebrate the hell out of it. We want to know what you're training for, when you're racing, where you're racing, and yes, we would very much like the opportunity to show up with signs and yell your name at an unreasonable volume.

So if you have anything on the calendar this fall, TELL US. Tell your coaches, email the Front Desk, send us the details. Big race, first race, 47th race, something completely outside your comfort zone—we want all of it.

Because PRs are cool. Watching your gym friends do hard things out in the wild is cooler.

CFNYC race season roll call: what are we training for?!
